title: Dim sum restaurant in Sugar Land
assumptions: The company still has to be formed (an LLC) unless an entity is named. Hires staff. Builds out the space. No new exterior sign (signage: false).

items.name: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
items.note: IRS: "You never have to pay a fee for an EIN."

items.name: Sales and Use Tax Permit
items.feeNote: No fee; a security may be required.
items.note: One permit for each active place of business.

items.name: Unemployment tax account
items.note: Register within 10 days of becoming liable.

items.name: Food handler training for food employees
items.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
items.note: Within 30 days of employment (§228.31); certified food managers exempt.

items.name: Assumed Name Certificate
items.condition: Only when trading under a name other than the legal name.

items.name: Certified food manager
items.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services (licensed programs); required on site by Houston Health
items.note: Houston's pre-operational inspection asks for the certified food manager's name.
items.quote: A minimum of one employee must have a valid Food Manager Certification during all hours of operation.

items.name: Food establishment plan review
items.agency: City of Sugar Land Permits Office
items.quote: Plan reviews are only accepted online through Citizen Self-Service (CSS) Portal.

items.name: Food permit
items.agency: City of Sugar Land Food Inspection Program
items.quote: Food permit application must be completed prior to requesting a final food inspection.

items.name: Certificate of Occupancy
items.agency: City of Sugar Land Permits Office
items.match: (certificate of occupancy).*(sugar land)|(sugar land).*(certificate of occupancy)
items.quote: the permits office will issue you a new Certificate of Occupancy via email.

items.name: Building permit for the build-out
items.agency: City of Sugar Land Permits Office
items.note: The pre-opening sheet covers the food steps; the building permit itself wasn't read.

order.why: IRS: "form your entity through the secretary of state before you apply for an EIN."
Plan review before construction; the food permit before the final inspection.

mustNotInclude.name: Houston's permits
mustNotInclude.why: Sugar Land runs its own permits.
